0.long_answer: Cowden syndrome is the hereditary syndrome characterized by hamartomatous gastrointestinal polyps and trichilemmomas, and it is associated with a mutation in the PTEN gene on chromosome 10q23.3. This syndrome is inherited in an autosomal dominant pattern and predisposes individuals to various benign and malignant tumors, including those in the thyroid, breast, kidney, and endometrium. It is distinct from other polyposis syndromes like Peutz-Jeghers syndrome, which is linked to mutations in the STK11 gene on chromosome 19.
